learning_outcomes.text: The student acquires insight into how numerical calculations are performed on a computer, including concepts such as approximation and rounding errors, numerical stability, condition, efficiency, etc.

The student learns about elementary solution methods for standard numerical problems such as: systems of linear and non-linear equations, polynomial interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration, ordinary differential equations, roots of functions, and optimization problems, particularly (non)linear least squares problems.
The implementation of these methods in numerical software is briefly covered.
Be able to recognize numerical sub-problems in a larger complex problem.
Be able to recognize difficult numerical problems (condition) and distinguish them from poor results obtained by unstable algorithms.
Be able to accurately describe a numerical solution method through a number of algorithmic steps (high-level and language-independent).
Be able to read simple Matlab programs and make changes.
Be able to interpret the numerical results of a computer program for their accuracy and explain any anomalies.
Be able to devise creative numerical and theoretical solutions for problems that are variants of what has been seen.
To some extent, be able to make a responsible choice from available numerical software to solve a problem.
Consider the possibility of a numerical solution in addition to the analytical solution of a problem with paper and pencil or with Maple.
Maintain a healthy skepticism towards numerical results obtained after long or even relatively short calculations.
Pay attention to efficiency and accuracy when designing a numerical solution method.
When tackling a numerical problem, first look for good available software before writing a program yourself.

syllabus_topics: Exercises on the material covered in the lecture
Deepening and applying Matlab knowledge as a programming language and environment
assessment_rules: The evaluation consists of a written exam during the examination period, covering both theoretical exercises and interpretations of numerical algorithms, their results, and Matlab code snippets.
